item.title: The Imitation Blob
item.description: My idea for my first SCP, one that humanizes the D-Class a little more by ironically, turning a D-Class into anything but a human.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Horror/Drama
Elevator Pitch: A Blob capable of transforming into anything in consumes, and the disaster that occurs when it eats a D-Class.
Central Narritve:
The Imatation Blob, found by the foundation playing in a
small puddle, it normal behavior is freindly and curious, until introduced to a living creature via touch.

Upon being exposed to a living creature, the blob will trap the hand or foot of its victim with it's super sticky body then being to slowly swell in size until it capable of absorbing its victim into its body. At which point it will encompass them and until they have been completely dissolved into the blobs Body.

The Blob will then transform into a perfect replica of it's victim and adopt the victims mannerisms until it eats something else, at which point it will revert back to it's base form and resume normal behavior. Despite this The Blob has shown no need for food or water and can survive just fine without it.

+ show block
– hide block

That's how it behaved before incident (insert number here).

After multiple test on the Blob, D-Class testing was approved, The Blob behaved exactly the same throughout most of the test, up until D-Class (insert number here) was fully consumed.

However instead of adopting the D-Classes appearance and behavior, it remained in it's blob form for 10 minutes, studying itself, seemingly confused about it's own body.
Afterwards The Blob transformed into a unknown creature and breached containment.

The Blob then proceeded to rampage through the site, taking the form of multiple creatures, many anomalous and previously unknown to the SCP foundation. Before a MTF squad managed to secure and recontain The Blob, it had killed multiple researchers and gaurds, and had even managed to absorb both an instance of SCP-939 and an instance of SCP-3199. Strangely, no D-Class were harmed during the breach, and The Blob seemed to target Security Gaurds and Reaserchers accompanied by D-Class above others.

The Blob now behaves extremely differently, it is aggressive and makes multiple attempts to breach containment every day. It has also begun to replicate 939 and use its ability to replicate human voices to communicate, although most of its vocabulary seems to consist of Explitives directed at Researchers.

This has led to the conclusion that instead of The Blob temporily replicating the physical appearence and behavior of the D-Class, it instead permanently replicate its behavior without replicating it's physical appearance, gaining sentience and a grudge against the foundation and it's personnel as well as a fondness and sense of comradery towards D-Class.

The Blob can also now control it's replication ability with relative ease. As such, it's containment procedures now require it be contained in a cell capable of containing as many different SCPs as possible, for it is unknown how many creatures The Blob is capable of replicating now.

In the event The Blob does breach containment, Security Gaurds are instructed to take as many D-class as possible into a secured intercom room. Then the Security Gaurds are instructed to threaten to terminate D-Class if The Blob does not return to containment, followed by terminate 1 D-Class every minute until The Blob returns to containment, a MTF squad arrives, or The Blob manages to gain access to the secured intercom room.

Attention Grabber: Basically, I find the potential for sympathetic or humanized D-Class severely underutilized and I wanted to show more of the comradery between the members of D-class. Plus the Idea of an SCP that could possibly become any other SCP Kinda freaks me out so I had to write it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 185 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: Critter Profile: Emma and Cream!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No, I already have pages up.

Page Type: GoI Format

Page Layout: A "password protected" link to click to reveal the page

Elevator Pitch: Emma the fire-spewing Texas horned lizard fares better when placed by Cream the goose who lays golden eggs — so much better, in fact, that she grows beyond her expected size. When a robber stops by to steal the goose, he gets more than he bargained for.

Central Narrative: Emma is a Texas horned lizard who shoots fire from her eyes instead of blood. She comes in clutching a gold ring, which is taken and sold, Wilson’s not realizing its importance. Emma then becomes smaller and more lethargic by the day, prompting concern from staff at Wilson's.

Cream is a goose who lays golden eggs which turn into normal eggs after a few hours. The page notes that there have been multiple inquiries and Cream is not up for adoption. When Cream gets transported past Emma’s terrarium for a checkup, Emma perks up and rushes to the front.

Wilson’s staff decide to put the two in enclosures next to each other and Emma starts healing with the proximity to gold. The two seem to like each other. Emma starts growing much larger than a horned lizard usually gets. Once she is large enough that her safety would no longer be a concern, Emma and Cream are placed together for short periods under close supervision. The two form a close bond, both showing signs of distress whenever they are separated.

In the email at the bottom, we learn of a Wilson’s overnight staff member hearing human screams along with distress calls from many of the animals. When they investigate, they find a robber who had tried to break into Cream's enclosure with a carrying cage. His hand is chewed off and he has severe burns all across his body. The lock to Emma's enclosure has melted open from the inside, but Emma is sitting inside near the wall that separates her from Cream. The robber is rushed to the hospital and the email suggests the web page be put under password protection in the future to avoid similar incidents — thus the password requirement at the beginning of the page.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Wilson's gets a sort-of dragon. Two animals make unlikely friends.

The being that is wearing the Crown is an Intelligent Turkish Angora Cat, and said Cat has taken over Site-33, turning it into his 'Palace'.

Central Narrative: Narrative will mostly revolve around how the Cat acquired the Crown, during a Site-Wide Containment Breach, and the aftermath. To explore on how the Crown has affected Site Personal, there will be MTF Logs, showing their mission to retake Site-33, and to recapture the anomalies.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Hook will be the initial SCP File, which is Site-33's version of the file edited by a Brainwashed Researcher, telling us how we should worship the Cat, and make offerings and/or sacrifices for it. After that, there will be the actual file from outside Site-33, describing the anomaly and how to contain it, along with the MTF Logs.

Additional Notes:I would like any advice on how the Foundation can counter the Brainwashing affect of the Crown, and if there is a specific terminology I can use. I know I probably need to expand on the Crown and how it really works. Also, if there is specific breed of Cat that you think would be more fitting, please tell me.

item.title: Blood Rose
item.description: A flower that smells so sweet, you'd bleed for it. Cognitohazardous plant.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Horror, History.

Page Layout: Simple Containment Procedures, followed by the description and discovery, an interview log, possibly research notes for additional findings, and maybe a test with the flower's scent.

Elevator Pitch: A flower, specifically a rose, that possesses an olfactory cognitohazard that causes anyone that smells it to self-harm and "water" it with there own blood, killing themselves.

Central Narrative: The Foundation learns that hikers and their search parties have continuously gone missing in a forest and send a team to investigate. They find a secluded part of the forest where a lone rose sits at the top of a small hill. All but one of the agents begin to cut themselves and bleed near the rose, remarking about it's beauty and it's sweet scent. The last agent, who has no sense of smell (anosmia), tries to stop the others from hurting themselves. He's attacked and runs away while being pursued by one of the agents, who later dies from blood loss. The incident report he gives later provides more detail about his experience. A second team arrives later to retrieve the flower and discover the hill it's on is filled with human bodies and skeletons, which they take samples from. The flower is moved to a Foundation site where it can be studied and no longer posses a threat to civilians.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: How the flower contains the human DNA of it's victims, and the history of all it's victims.

Additional Notes: I feel like this could possibly end in several different ways. Either the Foundation conducts tests with the flower's scent, or try to grow more, or some other third thing. Any suggestions? The story might be a bit lacking. Any thoughts on how to flesh it out more? The Hook could probably use some work as well. I really want to convey a slightly horrifying feeling as far as the "blood-watering" goes.

I want to hear any suggestions and criticism.

item.title: SCP - Kraken Mare
item.description: An anomalous ecosystem on Titan.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Science Fiction

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article.

Elevator Pitch: There's an alien ecosystem in Kraken Mare, the largest of Titan's liquid methane seas. The anomaly is that the life there isn't really alien at all - all the organisms there are copies of marine life from Earth's Cretaceous seas, modified on the chemical level to survive Titan's conditions but unchanged on the macro scale. So rather than aliens swimming in methane, there are mosasaurs and ammonites instead.

Central Narrative: The central narrative is the mystery of how prehistoric animals ended up living on Titan. The Foundation first found the anomaly when a NASA probe to Kraken Mare got eaten - containment focuses on keeping information from getting out rather than doing anything on Titan itself. Eventually the Foundation sends another probe to explore Kraken Mare. The exploration log ends with a plinth on the seafloor that lists the surface liquids and basic biochemical reactions found on Earth, Titan, and an unknown third world with sulfuric acid seas. The implication is that aliens copy-pasted an ecosystem from one liquid medium to another, and did the same elsewhere, for reasons unknown.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think it's a fun mix between aliens and dinosaurs, combining real-life sea monsters with exotic hypothetical biochemistry. The story also ends with the revelation that powerful anomalous beings once came to Earth and, for once, did something pretty benign.

Additional Notes: I'm thinking about having the plinth be written in Ortothan, just to tie the SCP into something bigger and make it feel more connected to some other space SCPs.

item.title: Men Are Expendable
item.description: "We do not need men anymore"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight : No (not yet)

Page Type : SCP Article

Genre : Drama

Elevator Pitch : An SCP that allows a woman to get pregnant without having any sexual intercourse with a man. The activation of the SCP’s abnormal properties requires a sacrifice consisting of human blood, water and animal bones. The SCP “steals” another woman's pregnancy in order to make the user pregnant, and children born this way might be “special”.

Narrative : (( I want to use the idea of fertility and pregnancy, and put it as the central abnormal effect of this SCP. This idea is inspired by an old African legend, in which a young infertile woman, Akua, was given a doll that would supposedly help her get pregnant ; which it did, or at least according to the legend. The doll was transmitted from woman to woman, and disappeared after some time. ))

+ show block
– hide block

The Foundation received reports of a secret tribe located somewhere in Africa, in which men and women were showing incredible physical and mental abilities (strength, logical thinking and great charisma). Its inhabitants didn’t show any sign of hostility towards the SCP Agents that were sent to the place.

Upon investigating, the Foundation discovered that the tribe worshipped a wooden doll. Thanks to the efforts of The Foundation’s Translators, the agents were able to engage in a discussion with the aborigens, and discovered the abnormal effects of the doll.
The resulting births and “procreation” within the tribe were hence caused by the impact of the SCP’s abnormal effects : all of the inhabitants claimed to have a woman as their parent, and the idea of a father seemed strange to them.
It was peculiar that the tribe was so sophisticated and well-developed, despite being isolated from the rest of the world (complex language, irrigation systems…).The way it managed to remain hidden, as well as its history remains unknown.

The wooden doll was recovered [stolen] by the Foundation in order to study its anomalous properties. This led to a battle, resulting in a total termination of the tribe’s members.

Hook/Attention-Grabber : I find this SCP interesting because it deals with the subject of fertility in a curious way.

Additional Notes : N/A

item.title: SCP: Older Brother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: nuclear "siblings"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Elevator Pitch: The first anomaly is a child in a hazmat suit who's composed of 40% of the same materials found in a hydrogen bomb. The child was discovered in an abandoned town in Northern Russia after reports of unusual levels of radiation.

Due to being highly radioactive, the Foundation but him in a secure steel room. Even with its suit, contact with it results in severe radiation poisoning. The anomaly appears to have 3rd degree burns across its body, although it claims to suffer no physical pain from the burns.

The child also carries a backpack with 10 out of ordered issues of the Incredible Hulk.

It claims that it was left behind by their "older brother" in the town. It also talks about how its "Mother" used to care for them but she soon died forcing the two to depart for a new home.

+ show block
– hide block

The older brother is the second anomaly. It is an entity described to have "white noise" and " a dark figure". The entity only appeared once to take back the hazmat child due to the Foundation's "mistreatment" of them. The entity emits extremely high levels of radiation even in a 1-mile radius. It also affects electronic devices and signals rendering them dysfunctional. The entity also seems to have a psychic connection to the child, demonstrated when the child warns the Foundation that he is coming to pick him up.

Central Narrative: A foundation researcher will interview the child and will learn things about his older brother and Mother. But as the interviews go on, it becomes increasingly that the child keeping secrets. The child will eventually alert the Foundation that their "older brother" will take them due to disliking how the Foundation is handling him. This will lead to an incident that causes the deaths of multiple personnel including the researcher who interviewed the child.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:I want this SCP to have layers of mystery like where these two came from and who "Mother" is within the interviews the child has with the researcher. But I also want to keep it vague enough to be left to interpretation. The older brother anomaly will also be shown through an incident log.

Additional Notes:

  • Their origins might be linked to Russian nuclear testing
  • The child is older than it seems
  • There's an important correlation between the Incredible Hulk comic and the pair that will be expanded on

item.title: Carnivorous Tattoo
item.description: What if your Tattoo wasn’t what it seemed?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-#### “The Predatory Tattoo” is entity in the form of a tattoo usually appearing to look like a predatory creature ranging from several present day predators to extinct/unknown species. It primarily targets individuals with atleast 3 or more tattoos but will on rare occasions appear on individuals with little to no tattoos. At first it’ll just be seen as a tattoo that the victim wouldn’t seem to have any memory of getting it. As time goes on the victim will notice slight imperfections with the tattoo, such as it seeming to be out of place and its eyes seeming to be looking up. Claw mark-like tattoos over existing tattoos/bare skin that seem to sting as would normal claw marks would also appear. Eventually it would kill its victim in the way the predator its based off would normally kill its prey (bruises associated with being constricted being tattooed on the victim or gashes from claws as well)

Central Narrative: the anomalous entity would first be discovered after the latest victim in a string of murder was brought to the attention of the foundation. Agents disguised as Federal agents would confiscate the recent body as well as all files on previous victims. After transferring the corpse to a foundation facility, one of the retrieval agents would discover an tattoo of unknown origin on his back after feeling a stinging sensation and seeing the scp taking the form of extinct species of Kaprosuchus. After the agents death from the scp, the skin of the agents back was removed, preserved and placed in a frame with the scp still in place with physical contact being heavily restricted to prevent containment breaches.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The ‘ink’ comprising of both the scp and the wounds it inflicts would contain partial dna mixed in with the normal content of the tattoo ink. Its main way of hunting would appear to try and make its prey paranoid all the while it toys with its prey.

Additional Notes: As stated, normal means one would take to remove a tattoo does not seem to work with the person attempting to remove the entity reporting feeling unnerved and/or receive tattooed markings in the form of self defensive slashes or bites

item.title: Random Access Memory
item.description: A usb flash drive seeking out data
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A USB flash drive that teleports from one data storage device to another

Central Narrative: A usb stick jumps from storage device to storage device to download random files. The usb stick starts out first with things like computers and servers, but changes to more forms of data storage, such as phones, alarm clocks, vending machines, electronic locks, and eventually brains. As it jumps from device to device, it attaches itself to anything that would contain data rather than to a port. This causes problems as, when it jumps, it will deform anything around it in order to fit into the device. This might mean cracking a casing or pushing away brain tissue. The usb stick was first found by an on-site tech repair team while examining a broken computer. Initially, it is relatively easy to contain by putting it into a secure storage locker, as it so far has only chosen computers. Containment becomes more complicated as it begins to attach itself to the electronic locks, cameras, and even occasionally other scps. Containment becomes vital when the usb begins to cause fatalities by inserting itself into brains. Eventually the containment consists of an empty room with one DC voltage light and a mechanical locked door with a viewing port and a telescope. New usbs with random data are pulled in via a pulley system using only rope and a hand crank. The nearest telephone is a rotary phone with no data storage whatsoever. Due to its lethality, researchers weren’t able to come up with an explanation as to what the USB’s function is, or where it came from.

item.title: Temporal Hula Hoops.
item.description: When an object passes through the hoop it is transported 10 minutes into the past or the future, depending on which side you go through.
item.content:encoded:
It is just a thing that does a thing, but I feel it's simple enough for it to be worthy of the site if nothing similar has been done before, the containment and testing logs will probably be more interesting than one may expect, for example, the hoop must be left idle for 10 minutes before and after testing due to the possibility of a D-Class using it to breach containment via going back in time to the point where the hoop is being transported to the testing room.

I also want to clarify that it isn't proper time travel, it works by transporting objects to an alternate dimension that was created exactly 10 minutes before or after the one you're currently in, with no other differences, I feel that this is a good way to get around the whole tricky paradox discussion.

I'm also considering having multiple hoops, having them test out what happens when you put a hoop into another hoop and then go through it, in a case like this the destination of the hoop inside the hoop will just be where it was 10 minutes ago from its perspective, consider the following test, at 0 minutes hoop A is introduced to the testing area, at 5 minutes hoop B2 exits hoop A (arriving from the future), hoop B2's destination will therefore be 10 minutes into the test (if going through it towards the past), an object A is put through hoop B2, then at 10 minutes into the test Hoop B1 is introduced into the testing area, object A instantly exits hoop B1 (arriving from the "future" from the hoops perspective, the past from an outside observers perspective.), at 15 minutes Hoop B1 is thrown through Hoop A, it's destination being at 5 minutes into the test, this concludes the test.

This is just what I had been considering while thinking of this idea, I think it's interesting enough to not simply be a "thing that does a thing" but others may not share the same opinion, what do you think?

item.title: Strict Stethoscope
item.description: A stethoscope that can detect medical maladies and hates prescription drug abuse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A sentient stethoscope capable of speech, with extensive knowledge of non-anomalous medical ailments, and human anatomy. The anomaly can accurately diagnose patients by sight alone, even if the affliction isn’t currently visible When an individual attempts to take any prescription medication that they are not currently prescribed, they will be compelled not to the first time, and the stethoscope will angrily inform them about the dangers of taking unprescribed medicine, and warn them not to. If the individual decides to take it anyway, they will gain a severe and often outlandish form of whatever ailment the medication treats. If they choose not to, a non-anomalous lollipop will materialize near the subject.

Central Narrative: The item is recovered from an otherwise normal hospital after reports from a nurse who attempted to abuse opiates while hiding in a storage closet. During recovery, the anomaly cries out in protest and then refuses to communicate until a researcher threatens to take Adderal during an interview. After learning they are conversing with a doctor, the anomaly opens up, detailing its creation. The item promises full cooperation so long as they are allowed to practice medicine or be in the vicinity of a clinic, as that is their sole purpose for existence. After being asked if they have ever signed a Hippocratic Oath, the item replies that they find it nonsensical, and instead signed an Oath of their own design, that allows them to punish patients for “failure to follow basic instructions or general stupidity,” among other things. A selection from the oath is engraved into the side of the anomaly, and a full paper copy is retrieved from the location the anomaly states it was created in. Several tests follow, wherein the item diagnoses several subjects with near-perfect success, and punishes subjects with effects that reciprocate the medications they take. After being presented with an individual afflicted by another SCP, the item expresses confusion, and is unable to diagnose, or offer any treatment. After proving itself, the item is transferred to Site 20 to aid in medical duties.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The secondary anomalous effects are dark, with a small hint of humor. I thought it’d be neat.

Additional Notes: None

Originally the foundation was fine with discretely relocating the animals to a natural habitat, until during a surgical inspection one started speaking, talking of biblical anomalies and telling the foundation they should just let the cavern make life. After this, the foundation started killing all the new specimens, in fear all of them are unnoticeably anomalous.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's short, sweet, and too the point. It tells the story and leaves the mystery. Think of it like a different take on SCP-2000: an anomaly that (for the most part) creates normal life, but the foundation decides to contain it as they understand it even less.
